title: Using a 3‑in‑1 Avocado Tool to Create Avocado‑Infused Hummus
meta_description: Level up your dip game! Learn how to use an avocado slicer for avocado hummus to create a creamy, healthy snack without the kitchen accidents.
html:
There is nothing quite like the creamy satisfaction of a fresh batch of hummus, but if you are looking to add a layer of richness and a boost of healthy fats, adding avocado is the way to go. The only problem? Dealing with avocados can be a gamble. Between the slippery skin and the stubborn pit, it is far too easy to slip with a chef's knife. That is why I always reach for my avocado slicer avocado hummus prep method to keep things safe and efficient.

Why Use an Avocado Slicer Tool for Hummus?

When you are making a dip, you don't necessarily need perfectly uniform cubes, but you do need the fruit out of the skin quickly and safely. The Avocado Slicer Tool is a game-changer here because it handles the three most annoying parts of the process: splitting, pitting, and slicing.

Using a traditional knife to scoop out avocado often results in wasted fruit left on the skin or, worse, a trip to the first-aid kit. The 3-in-1 design allows you to glide the blade around the pit and scoop out clean slices that drop right into your food processor, minimizing cleanup and maximizing your yield.

Gathering Your Ingredients

To make a balanced avocado-infused hummus, you want to maintain that classic garlicky tang while letting the avocado provide the buttery texture. Here is what you will need:

Step-by-Step: Avocado Slicer Avocado Hummus Prep

The secret to a smooth dip is how you handle the produce. Start by using the splitting edge of the Avocado Slicer Tool to cut a clean line around the circumference of the avocado. Twist and pull the halves apart.

Next, use the pitting feature to safely pop the seed out. No more hacking at the pit with a knife and hoping for the best. Once the pit is gone, use the slicing fan to create even strips of avocado. This ensures that the fruit is broken down quickly in the processor, preventing any large, unblended chunks of avocado from streaking through your hummus.

Toss the slices into your food processor along with the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and cumin. Pulse until the mixture is thick, then slowly drizzle in olive oil or water while the motor is running until you reach your desired creaminess.

Tips for the Perfect Consistency

Avocados vary in water content, so always taste and texture-test your hummus before adding too much liquid. If your avocado was exceptionally ripe, you might find you don't need any extra oil at all. The natural fats from the fruit often replace the need for heavy amounts of tahini or oil.

To keep the hummus from browning, make sure your lemon juice is fresh. The citric acid acts as a natural preservative. If you are storing the dip for a few days, press a piece of plastic wrap directly onto the surface of the hummus before sealing the lid; this removes the oxygen that causes oxidation.

Serving and Pairing Ideas

Once your avocado hummus is blended, transfer it to a bowl and create a swirl with a spoon. Drizzle a bit of extra virgin olive oil on top and sprinkle with paprika or toasted sesame seeds for a professional look.

This dip pairs beautifully with crisp vegetable sticks like carrots, cucumbers, and bell peppers. Because of the added creaminess from the avocado, it also works exceptionally well as a spread for toasted sourdough or as a base for a Mediterranean-style wrap with grilled chicken and feta cheese.

FAQ

Can I use a frozen avocado with the Avocado Slicer Tool?

No, the Avocado Slicer Tool is designed for fresh, ripe avocados. Frozen avocados usually come pre-cubed or mashed, and the structure is too soft for the slicing fan to work effectively.

How long does avocado hummus stay fresh in the fridge?

Because of the fresh avocado, this hummus has a shorter shelf life than traditional chickpea hummus. It generally stays fresh for 3 to 5 days if stored in an airtight container with plastic wrap pressed against the surface.

What if my avocado is too firm to slice?

If the avocado is too hard, the slicing tool may struggle to glide through. If you're in a rush, you can place the avocado in a brown paper bag with a banana for 24 hours to speed up the ripening process before using your tool.
